transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's very nice to meet you too, Doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. I, um... well, I hope I'm not wasting your time with this. It's probably nothing major, just... I guess I keep messing up little things lately. 

Nothing terrible, you know, just sort of silly mistakes that make me feel a bit foolish. Like, I'll write down the completely wrong time on a class sheet over at the senior center. Or... well, I like to tinker with things, and I'll measure a piece of wood, but I guess I just kind of skip over the small print or the little marks on the tape, and I still end up cutting the board a hair short. 

It's a little embarrassing to even bring up, to be honest, because I know I should be paying better attention. Does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing I should be telling you?
When these mistakes happen, do you have trouble seeing small print or fine markings clearly?

Oh, no, no, my eyesight is perfectly fine, thankfully. I have reading glasses, of course, but I use them. It's not that I can't see the little marks, it's just... I don't know, I guess I just look right past them sometimes? Or I glance at it and think I've got it right, but I don't. It's just me being careless, really. I hope that's helpful? I'm sorry if I wasn't clear before.
Have you been having trouble remembering recent conversations or appointments?

Oh, um, no, not really. I mean, I think my memory is still pretty sharp for a guy my age. I haven't missed any appointments or forgotten anything important like that. I always make sure to write things down on my calendar, so I'm usually right on top of it. I might occasionally forget where I put my keys for a minute, but everyone does that, right? It's nothing serious. I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answers? I just want to make sure I'm doing this correctly.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even about everyday things?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I'm actually a pretty calm fellow, mostly. I don't really sit around fretting about everyday stuff. I mean, I want things to go well, of course, but I just try to take life one day at a time. 

I get a little frustrated with myself when I make those careless mistakes we talked about, sure, but it's not like a big worry that keeps me up at night or anything. I hope that's... is that a good thing? Am I explaining that alright for you?
Have these mistakes started to make it harder for you to manage your usual daily activities on your own?

Well, um... I wouldn't say it's made things *harder* exactly. I can still do most everything I need to do. It's just... well, I guess I have stepped back a little bit from helping lead those DIY workshops at the community center. Just a couple of them. I didn't want my little mix-ups to cause any trouble for the other folks, you know? 

And, well, my wife has started double-checking our plans a bit more lately. Just to make sure I don't accidentally throw off the timing for family visits or when we go to the center. She's wonderful about it, really. It's just a little extra help so I don't mess up anyone else's schedule. That's not too unusual for someone my age, is it? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
Compared with a year or two ago, do you feel less able to pay close attention to details?

Oh, well... no, I don't think so. I feel like my attention to detail is about the same as it's always been, really. I mean, maybe I'm a tiny bit slower at reading through the newspaper than I was a couple of years ago, but I still catch everything I need to. I don't feel like I'm missing the fine print or anything like that. I think I'm doing pretty well for 62, don't you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need. Is that the sort of thing you were looking for?
Are you still able to manage your finances on your own?

Oh, yes, absolutely. I still handle all the bills and the, um, the checkbook. My wife leaves all of that to me, actually. 

I mean, I might take an extra minute to double-check my addition every now and then, just to be perfectly safe, but I haven't missed any payments or gotten confused by the bank statements or anything like that. I keep everything pretty tidy in that department. So, no problems there... which is a good sign, right? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of details here.
Has your wife told you that your thinking or concentration seems worse than it used to be?

Oh, no... no, she hasn't said anything like that at all. 

I mean, like I mentioned, she's been helping out a little with the calendar and the plans, but she's never actually sat me down and said my concentration is getting worse or that my thinking is slipping. She's very sweet about everything. I think she knows I'm just... well, just being me, you know? 

We communicate really well, so I'm sure she would tell me if she was truly worried about my mind. That's a good thing, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture here. Am I answering these the right way for you?
Compared with a few years ago, do you feel your thinking has gotten worse?

Oh, no, I don't believe so. My mind feels just about as clear as it did a few years back, really. 

I mean, maybe I pause to find a word every now and then, but nothing out of the ordinary for a guy my age, you know? My actual reasoning and how I think through things... that all feels perfectly fine to me. I don't feel like I've lost a step there at all. 

So, I'd have to say no, it hasn't gotten worse. Is that... does that answer your question alright? I just want to be sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to know.
Has anyone close to you, like your wife, told you that you’ve been making more mistakes than you used to?

Oh, goodness, no. No, she definitely hasn't said anything like that. 

I mean, I try really hard to make sure I do things right around the house so she doesn't have to worry. If I ever, you know, drop the ball on a little chore or forget to put something away, it's just a normal little oversight. Nothing she'd call a pattern of mistakes, and certainly not worse than before. She's never complained about me messing things up, thank heavens. I think I do a pretty good job keeping on top of my end of things. 

Is that... does that help? I really hope I'm giving you the kind of information you need to hear.
Have you yourself noticed any change in your thinking abilities compared with how you used to be?

No, I really haven't. I feel like I'm just as sharp as I've always been, to be perfectly honest. 

I mean, sure, maybe I don't read as fast as I did in my twenties, or I might take a second longer to figure out the remote control, but my actual thinking? The way I put thoughts together? That hasn't changed a bit. I still feel very capable and clear-headed. I wouldn't want you to think my mind is going or anything like that. 

I feel like I'm doing really well for my age. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers so you can do your job.
Has your wife noticed that you’ve become more forgetful or made more mistakes than you used to?

Well, no, not at all. Like I think I mentioned just a moment ago, she really hasn't said anything about me making mistakes or forgetting things. 

I mean, sure, maybe I'll misplace my reading glasses every now and then, or forget why I walked into the kitchen, but who doesn't at 62, right? It's just normal everyday stuff. It's certainly nothing that's bothered her or made her think I'm slipping. I really do try my best to keep on top of everything around the house so she doesn't have to stress about me. 

I know you just asked something kind of similar, so I hope it's okay that my answer is pretty much the same. I'm just trying to be as honest as I can for you. Am I doing alright with these questions? I want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Has anyone at the senior center told you that you've been making more mistakes there than you used to?

Oh, heavens no. The folks down at the center... no, they haven't said a word like that to me. We mostly just, you know, play cards or sit and chat, and I always make sure I'm paying close attention so I don't hold up the games. I'd be absolutely mortified if I was making mistakes and ruining things for everyone else. 

If anything, I try to be the one helping out—setting up the chairs, getting the coffee ready, that sort of thing. I really try to be a good neighbor there and pull my weight. 

I know I keep giving you the same sort of 'no' answer to these last few questions... I hope that's not frustrating for you? I promise I'm not trying to be difficult, I'm just trying to give you the honest truth. Am I still doing okay with all this? I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient for you.
Has your wife started checking your calendar and plans more often because she has noticed you making mistakes?

Well... gosh. I suppose when you ask about the calendar specifically like that... I want to be completely open with you, doctor. She... she has started double-checking our plans a little bit lately. Just to make sure I don't accidentally throw off the timing for when the family comes to visit, or when I'm supposed to be at the center. It's really just her being sweet and helpful, you know? 

And... well, I guess I did decide to step back from helping lead a couple of the DIY workshops down at the center recently. Just because of a few minor mix-ups on my end. Nothing terrible at all! I just figured it was better to let someone else take the lead rather than risk messing up the schedule for the rest of the group. 

I'm so sorry I didn't mention that a moment ago when you asked about mistakes. I guess I was just a little embarrassed to admit it out loud, and I really don't want you to think poorly of me. I hope you're not upset with me for holding that back at first? I promise I'm really trying my best to give you the right answers.
Do you now need help with everyday tasks that you used to do completely on your own?

Oh, no, definitely not. I'm still doing everything I've always done. I mean, sure, my wife might remind me about an appointment here or there, like we just talked about, but as far as getting dressed, making my meals, taking care of myself... I handle all of that just fine on my own. 

I'd hate to be a burden on anyone, especially her. I really make a point to keep up with my own chores and routines so she doesn't have to worry about me in that way. I'm still very capable of looking after myself, I promise. 

I hope I'm giving you the kind of information you need? I want to make sure I'm answering these right for you.
Has your wife told you that your memory or thinking has gotten worse over the past year or two?

Oh, gosh, no. She hasn't said anything like that at all. I mean... I know we just talked about her checking the calendar, and I really appreciate you being so patient with me about that. But as far as my actual memory or... or my brain getting worse? No, definitely not. 

She knows I've always been just a little bit, well, easily side-tracked, but my mind is still perfectly sound. I read the paper, I keep up with the news... I really try to stay sharp so she doesn't ever have to worry about me in that way. 

I hope I'm explaining the difference okay? I don't want to sound like I'm contradicting myself after admitting the thing about the schedule. I just want to be as helpful and accurate as possible for your notes. Am I still giving you what you need?
Has your wife noticed that you’re not as sharp as you used to be?

Well... no, she hasn't said anything like that. I know it sounds a lot like what you just asked, and I hope I'm not being difficult by giving the same sort of answer. But really, she hasn't mentioned me losing my edge or anything like that. 

I mean, I'm 62, so maybe I'm not quite as quick as I was in my twenties, but I think that's just normal getting older, right? My wife still talks things over with me just like she always has, and she certainly hasn't acted like I can't keep up with our conversations. I really try to stay engaged and present with her. 

I hope that makes sense? I'm trying my best to give you the whole picture without making things sound worse than they are. Am I doing okay with these questions?
Has your wife actually told you that she thinks your memory or thinking has declined?

Oh, dear... um, I feel like I might be frustrating you a bit since we keep coming back to this, and I'm really sorry if I'm not giving you the answer you need. I hope I'm not misunderstanding you. 

But... no, she truly hasn't ever said anything like that to me. I promise I'm not trying to hide anything from you. She knows I can be a little scattered sometimes, sure, but she's never sat me down and told me she thinks my mind is actually declining or failing. 

I hope it's alright that my answer is still no to this? I just really want to make sure I'm doing a good job for your evaluation and being as honest as I can.
Has your wife noticed that you make more mistakes than you used to?

Um... no, she hasn't said anything about me making more mistakes, either. I... I really hope I'm not being a difficult patient by saying no again. I know you're just being thorough, and I appreciate that, I really do. 

I mean, sure, I might misplace my glasses or, you know, forget why I walked into a room every now and then, but... but that's always been me. It's nothing new, and it's certainly not getting worse. I try really hard to double-check things so I don't make mistakes that affect her. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have a different answer for you? I'm really trying to be helpful and give you exactly what you need for your assessment. Am I still doing alright?
Could I speak with your wife about whether she has noticed any changes in your thinking?

Oh, um... well, yes, of course you can speak with her if you think that's necessary. I don't want to stand in the way of your process at all. I want to be as cooperative as possible. 

I just... I hope you don't think I'm trying to hide anything by saying she hasn't noticed changes. I'm really not. I just don't think she'll have much to tell you that's different from what I've said. But if it helps you do your job better, then absolutely, I can ask her to come in or give you a call. 

Is that what usually happens in these evaluations? I just want to make sure I'm following all the right steps for you.
